task.title: Home Timeline
task.statement: Design the home timeline for a social app: users follow other users, and opening the app shows recent posts from the people they follow, newest-ish first. Posts are mostly text plus images. Design both the write path (a post is published) and the read path (a user opens their feed).
task.notes:
Constraints — reveal ONLY if asked, one short sentence each:
1. How many users, and how much posting and reading? -> 50M daily actives out of 300M monthly; ~5K posts/sec written at peak, and ~50K feed-load QPS at peak — heavily read-dominated.
2. How fast must a feed load? -> p99 under 200ms for the first page of the feed.
3. What does the follow graph look like? -> Median user follows ~200 people and has ~100 followers, but celebrity accounts exist with up to 50M followers.
4. How fresh must the feed be? -> A new post should reach followers' feeds within ~30 seconds; strict global ordering is not required.
5. Is ranking in scope? -> Assume reverse-chronological with room to plug in a ranker later — the ML ranking model itself is out of scope.
If asked for a number not listed: tell them to pick one and defend it.

Stage probes (the clock marks tell you which stage you are in):
- requirements: They should establish the read-heavy ratio, the freshness tolerance (30s changes everything — it permits async fan-out), and above all ask about follower-count distribution. The celebrity skew is the crux of this problem; a candidate who never asks about it will design something that falls over, so if it hasn't come up by the end of requirements, ask 'does anyone here have a lot of followers?' and note that you had to.
- high_level: Sketch must contain: fan-out-on-write (push post IDs into per-follower feed lists at publish time) vs fan-out-on-read (query followees at read time) stated as an explicit tradeoff, the hybrid — push for normal users, pull for celebrity posts merged at read time; a feed store (e.g. capped per-user ID lists in Redis) distinct from the post store; image delivery via CDN kept out of the feed hot path; cursor-based pagination.
- deep_dive: Go deep on the hybrid fan-out. Hard questions: where exactly is the celebrity cutoff and what drives it (do the math — a 50M-follower post is 50M list-writes if pushed); and walk the read path precisely: fetch the materialized feed, fetch recent posts from the user's followed celebrities, merge by time, hydrate post bodies — all under 200ms p99. Ask what's stored in the feed list (IDs only, and why not full bodies) and how the capped list interacts with a user who scrolls deep.
- scale: 10x question: a global event — everyone posts at once and the fan-out workers develop a multi-minute backlog; how does staleness degrade, what do they shed or degrade first, and how would they even detect it (lag metric per queue). Failure question: the feed cache cluster is lost — feeds can be rebuilt from the follow graph and post store, but rebuilding 50M feeds is a thundering herd; what does the degraded read path serve in the meantime (pull-based fallback, capped)?

Challenge on sight (vague claims): Fan-out-on-write for everyone without confronting the 50M-writes-per-celebrity-post amplification.; "Just JOIN follows with posts at read time" without the query-cost math at 50K feed loads/sec against a 300M-row follow table.; "Kafka will handle it" as the entire answer to fan-out — no consumer scaling, partitioning, or backlog/lag discussion.; "Use a graph database" for what is a single-hop adjacency-list lookup.; Offset-based pagination on a feed that mutates between pages — duplicates and gaps — instead of cursor/timestamp-based.; Materializing full post bodies into every follower's feed list instead of IDs plus hydration — storage blow-up and stale-edit anomalies.
